title: fix(sse): streaming chunking/framing partial-JSON delimiter + token/event ordering
author: Maya Chen
description: Fixes a class of SSE streaming bugs observed with partial JSON payloads and function-calling/tool tokens where delimiter tokens and token/event ordering could be emitted out-of-order during chunking and framing. Root causes: incorrect boundary handling in the framer when streaming partial tokens across chunk boundaries, a race in the SSE emitter that reordered token events when backpressure triggered chunk coalescing, and an OpenAI-compat path that assumed delimiter tokens would always be emitted before token events. This change unifies framing logic, moves delimiter insertion to a single canonical point, adds a small state machine to preserve token/event ordering across chunk boundaries, and hardens the emitter to avoid coalescing races under backpressure. Also adds regression tests that replay production SSE traces and extends the openai_compat adapter to treat delimiter markers as first-class streaming events. See commits and changelist for details.

diff_snippets: framer.cc: inserted state machine to atomically track {IN_CHUNK, EMITTING_DELIMITER, EMITTING_TOKEN, FLUSH} and ensure delimiter events are emitted before tokens.
emitter.cc: added compare-and-swap guard when coalescing chunks under backpressure to preserve event ordering and avoid dropping delimiter markers.
streaming_adapter.py: changed delimiter handling from comment-style insert to explicit StreamingEvent.delimiter() and updated event serialization path.
review_comments: Alex Rivera: Found a race during the unit test that surfaced when multiple streams share the same emitter pool; recommended adding a CAS and a small sleep in the test to reproduce the original flakiness.
Maya Chen: responded - added CAS in emitter and added deterministic scheduler in the test to avoid non-deterministic sleeps.
Priya Singh: Suggested tightening the framer invariants and adding an assertion in debug builds when delimiter appears after a token in the same chunk.
Maya Chen: added the debug assertion and a focused integration test that replays the production trace where we previously saw out-of-order delimiters.
Tomás Blanco: approved with minor nits; asked to include a regression entry in release notes and to run perf canary to confirm no latency regression due to state machine.
